finding: Family is one base mob class plus one sprite sheet; a variant is a subclass that changes one frame block (rat +16/+32, gnoll +21/+42, mimic +16/+32/+48) and one on-hit effect (albino rat bleed, caustic slime ooze). Read in actors/mobs and sprites/.
Spawn rotation swaps a slot to its variant at 1 in 50 times an exotic multiplier; 11 base-to-variant pairs in the MobSpawner static block (actors/mobs/MobSpawner.java lines 245-274).

Depth scaling is a formula per family with a floor: mimic HP grows with level, piranha HP/defence/attack/damage grow with depth, elementals step by a region scale never below 2. Values are code, not donor data.
Dwarf king summons are nested subclasses of base mobs (ghoul, monk, warlock, golem), so the boss brings known creatures; read from class declarations only, bodies not read.
Look test: four creatures on one 375 screen (base vermin, pale bleed variant, elemental tint, mimic prop); can Dom name the family in one second and read the variant tag without text?

Species list is 102 species plus Invalid in one enum; per-species rows are not in the repo (Database/Base/WorldBase.sql is schema only: 29 CREATE TABLE, 0 INSERT), so no family or monster counts are claimed.

Each creature carries body parts with 25 fields (damage, variance, armour per damage type, hit-height weight, twelve hit-zone weights); an attack cone names one part, which gives a three-zone telegraph option for a phone.
Palette template and shade set the look and are copied to the corpse on death; shade on treasure create-list rows doubles as a 0-1 drop probability (Creature_Equipment around line 651).
Licence is AGPL v3 code with no asset licence and no client data in the repo; use the telegraph and corpse-look ideas at category level only, no species names or donor values.
